a:r.a:t: Structure of a Leucine Zipper: GCN4 from Yeast

p:cNvPr.descr: Two distinct structures illustrating leucine zippers. The first one shows four rows of letters, shown in sections, labeled DNA-binding region, connector (6 amino acids), and leucine zipper. These sections are all part of the amino acid sequence. To the left of these letters are two columns; the first is “Source,” and the second is “Regulatory protein.” The first three rows of letters all have “Mammal” as a source. The first one is C/EBP, which has the following letters in the DNA-binding region: DKNSEYRVRR (RR is shaded yellow) ER (R is shaded yellow) N (shaded orange) NIAVRK (K is shaded yellow) SR (R is shaded yellow) DK (K is shaded yellow) A. In the connector (6 amino acids) section is KQRNVE. In the leucine zipper section is TQQKVLEL (L is shaded red) TSDNDRL (L is shaded red) RKRVEQL (L is shaded red) SRELDTL (L is shaded red) RG-. Below that is Jun, which has a DNA-binding region with the following letters: SQERIKAERKR (KR shaded yellow), MR (R shaded yellow), N (shaded orange), RIAASK (K shaded yellow) CR (R shaded yellow), KRK (RK shaded yellow). The connector section is LERIAR. The leucine zipper section is L (shaded red) EEKVKTL (L shaded red) KAQNSEL (L shaded red) ASTANML (L shaded red), TEQVAQL (L shaded red) KQ-. The next row is Fos and has the following letters at the DNA-binding region: EERRRIRRIRR (RR shaded yellow) ER (R shaded yellow) N (shaded orange) KMAAAK (K shaded yellow) CR (R shaded yellow) NRR (RR shaded yellow). The connector section has RELTDT. The leucine zipper has L (shaded red) QAETDQL (L shaded red) EDKKSAL (L shaded red) QTEIANL (L shaded red) LKEKEKL (L shaded red) EF-. The next row has yeast as its source, and the regulatory protein is GCN4, which has the following DNA-binding region: PESSDPAALKR (KR shaded in yellow) AR (R shaded yellow) N (shaded orange) TEAARR (R shaded yellow) SR (R shaded yellow) ARK (RK shaded yellow). The connector section is LQRMKQ. The leucine zipper is L (shaded red) EDKVEEL (L shaded red) LSKNYHL (L shaded red) KKLVGER. This last row has two few letters at the end and no – symbol. Below these four rows is a row of dashes; however, under the sections of the letters that are shaded, the dashes skip. Below this is a row, labeled as consensus sequence. This starts out with 9 dashes, followed by R on top of K, R on top of K, a dash, R on top of K, an N, five dashes, R on top of K, a dash, R, a dash, R on top of K, R on top of K, six dashes, an L, six dashes, another L, six dashes, another L, six dashes, an L, six dashes, and an L. All the R on top of K’s are shaded yellow, the R is shaded yellow, the N is shaded orange and labeled Invariant Asn, and the Ls are shaded red. Below this is part b, which shows two blue strands forming a DNA double helix with blue pentagons hanging all around them. From top to bottom, the double helix forms one half-opened loop at the top, followed by two closed loops and another half-loop on the bottom. The line from the orange-shaded N points down to an orange structure in the center of the first full loop (this is the Invariant Asn). The orange is on one of the coils of a white ribbon. To the left of this is a yellow segment on the same coil. The rest of the coil is white (with a little yellow in the middle), and extends right, where it has some red shadings at some of the top coils. A similar coiled structure starts from the bottom left of the double helix and crosses the center all the way up to the right, where it intersects with the first coiled structure and creates a “zipper region” along the sections where both coils have red threads. Where the coils are orange and yellow (on the left) is labeled as the DNA-binding region.
